title: Cytoplasm: The Cell's Jelly
description: Inside every cell is a busy jelly where life happens. Explore the cytoplasm to claim piece 7.

content.value: Inside the cell membrane is a jelly-like substance called CYTOPLASM. It fills most of the cell and is where all the tiny cell structures float. Think of it as the 'living jelly' that holds everything in place.

The cytoplasm is not just filler — it is where many of the cell's chemical activities take place. Floating within it are the tiny ORGANELLES ('little organs'), each doing a special job for the cell. You'll meet them soon.

A CELL, from outside in:
🔲  cell membrane  (boundary / gatekeeper)
🟡  cytoplasm      (jelly where organelles float)
⚫  nucleus        (control centre)

Just as your body has organs (heart, lungs, stomach), a cell has tiny structures called ORGANELLES suspended in the cytoplasm. Each organelle carries out a particular function that keeps the cell alive. The cytoplasm is their home.
Picture a cell like a water balloon: the skin is the membrane, the water inside is the cytoplasm, and floating bits inside are the organelles — with the nucleus as the control centre.

Key Takeaway: Cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance inside the cell membrane where the cell's activities happen and the tiny organelles float. The three basic cell parts are membrane, cytoplasm and nucleus.

quiz.question: Cytoplasm is…
options: the jelly-like substance inside the cell membrane
the outer boundary of the cell
quiz.explain: Cytoplasm is the jelly that fills the cell inside the membrane, where organelles float.

quiz.question: The tiny structures floating in the cytoplasm that each do a special job are called…
quiz.explain: Organelles ('little organs') are the specialised structures in the cytoplasm.

quiz.question: The three basic parts of a cell are the cell membrane, the nucleus, and the…
quiz.explain: Nearly all cells have a membrane, cytoplasm and nucleus as their three basic parts.
